title: Baha (another version: Bata)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Temurah 29a: “Baha said that Rabbi Yochanan said: until they feed it vetch used for idolatry.” Rabbi Abba said to Baha: “Do you disagree with Ulla?” He said, “No.” Rabbi Abba said: “Baha knows how to resolve teachings; had he not gone up there he would not have known; the Land of Israel caused it for him.” Rabbi Yitzchak said: “Baha from here and from there” (that he studied both in Babylonia and in the Land of Israel — source abbreviation ר״נ).

notes.text: The vetch is used for idolatry, not simply owned by a gentile. The source’s closing ר״נ remains literal and unresolved, replacing the unsupported definite Rabbeinu Gershom attribution. Saved Rashi on Temurah 29a explains “from here and there” as Babylonia and the Land of Israel; saved Rabbeinu Gershom gives the same educational sense but names Rav Nachman in the exchange, while saved Davidson has Rav Yitzchak. These are separate witnesses, not proof of the intended abbreviation. The notice stays held.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. I, p. 262) ends the parenthetical gloss with ר״ג, where the supplied transcription has ר״נ. The consulted Rabbeinu Gershom on Temurah 29a explains that he studied in Babylonia and in the Land of Israel. The commentator’s text names Rav Nachman and uses the form באתא. The consulted Davidson text names Rav Yitzchak and has Baha. Rashi’s gloss explicitly gives both regions. These are readings of the specific witnesses.
